scene.note: One loop at the desk, and the rules handed to it as values: written, joined or named in a word.

steps.note: Ossian hands the desk a rule, such as children only, or a fare.
The desk asks the rule about each ticket of the day, once, in order.
The tickets the rule says yes to, or each ticket's fare, go on a new list. The day's tickets stay as they were.
Two rules become one that says yes only when both do, and stops at the first no.
A fare becomes a new fare with the harbour's fee on top.
The desk uses the joined rule and the new fare like any other.
Numbers written as text are read by a method that already exists.
A list of names answers whether a name is on it, and a ticket gives its passenger.
A fresh list is made each time one is asked for, and each of these goes to work where a rule is wanted.
